## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Kaṇhadīpāyanacariya* (Cp 31) is a verse narrative in the *Cariyāpiṭaka* recounting a past life of the Bodhisatta as the ascetic Kaṇha-Dīpāyana [SuttaCentral; Bareau]. In this birth, he maintained the conduct of an ascetic for more than fifty years despite having no delight in the hermit life [Bareau].

SuttaCentral lists three modern translations in three languages, including an English translation by Bhikkhu Sujato under the title *The Conduct of Kaṇhadīpāyana* [SuttaCentral]. A French translation and comparative study of the opening verse is provided by André Bareau [Bareau].

According to DharmaNexus, the text shares significant textual material with its commentary, the *Cariyāpiṭaka-aṭṭhakathā* (23 matching passages), as well as four verse passages with the canonical *Kaṇhadīpāyanajātaka* (Ja 444, particularly §11.1–12.3 sharing verses with Ja 444 §1.1–1.7) and three passages with the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus detects no cross-language matches with Chinese, Sanskrit, or Tibetan corpora with a score of 10 or greater, and SuttaCentral identifies no external parallels [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus].
